# ms: # One turn that called a tool. Two facts, both load-bearing.
# FIRST: no permission, approval, or prompt event of any kind appears anywhere in
# this run. The interval is delimited by recorded rows rather than by a watch --
# before_agent_start opens it and agent_settled closes it, with
# tool_execution_start and tool_execution_end inside -- so no capture window is
# owed and none is claimed. The tool was a bash command and it ran
# unconditionally. Pi ships no permission system, which is why blocked_on_request
# and unblocked are structurally unreachable rather than merely untraced.
# Be precise about what this does NOT show, because an earlier version of this
# note overreached. Pi's untyped event bus is not in these columns at all. The
# tracer that produced this file listened on sidecar:blocked and herdr:blocked
# and neither fired, but nothing here distinguishes "subscribed and saw nothing"
# from "never subscribed", so that is a fact about a run rather than evidence in
# a fixture, and it is not what the unreachability claim rests on. What it rests
# on is the emitter side, checkable without this file: the string "herdr" does
# not appear in pi 0.84.3's shipped bundle; ExtensionAPI.on enumerates thirty
# events and not one is a permission, approval or prompt event
# (types.d.ts:892-928); and Herdr's own four occurrences of its channel name are
# two listeners and two test drivers, with no publisher anywhere in its tree.
# SECOND: turn_start and turn_end each fire TWICE inside this single agent run,
# once around the tool call and once around the reply that followed it. A turn
# in Pi's vocabulary is a provider round trip, not a user-visible turn, so
# turn_end cannot be turn completion. agent_settled fires once, at the end, and
# that is why it is the only event the asset closes a turn on.
# tool_execution_start and tool_execution_end do fire and carry toolName, so
# tool_use is unclaimed by choice rather than by absence: the asset subscribes
# to neither, because tool use is a refinement of work_start rather than a lane.
